newsitem.title: SPAIN: American to buy 10 pct of Argentine airline.
newsitem.headline: American to buy 10 pct of Argentine airline.

text.p: Spain said Friday that flagship airline Iberia has signed key alliances with American Airlines and British Airways, including the sale of a 10 percent stake in Argentina's national carrier to American.

Iberia, on the verge of collapse just two years ago amid high costs and souring Latin American investments, had owned 85 percent of Aerolineas Argentinas. After selling a 10 percent stake to American, a unit of AMR Corp., it will sell much of its remaining holding in the airline, keeping only 10 percent.

State holding group Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales, or SEPI, said both American and British Airways have an option to buy a minority stake in Iberia by Dec. 31, kicking off the state-owned group's privatisation, SEPI said.

"(This will) strengthen (Iberia's) market position at home, assuring and extending its leadership in traffic between Europe and Latin America, as well as increasing its presence in the European, North Atlantic and Asian markets," SEPI said.
Both commercial deals foresee the establishment of agreements on code-sharing, frequent-flyer programmes, cargo operations and other areas where services can be improved.
"The agreements, once developed, will permit Iberia to increase its offer of flights and international connections... in what will be one of the world's biggest networks of global routes," SEPI said.
Iberia, which has faced a rocky road to renewed profitability, turned a profit of 3.5 billion pesetas ($23.2 million) in 1996 after reporting a loss the year before.
"It (the agreements) can only be good news. It might be a stimulus to move the Iberia project forward," an analyst in Madrid said.

At the end of June, Iberia Chairman Xavier de Irala said Iberia was speaking with British Airways, Air France, KLM, Swissair and Alitalia on a European alliance, but apparently opted for the group that had been most exposed to fierce international competition.
For its U.S. alliance, Iberia was also considering a deal with Continental Airlines, SEPI said this spring.

"BA is twice the size of Iberia in terms of passenger carriers...American overall is the second largest in the world," said Kevin Fogarty, transport analyst at Daiwa Europe in London. "What (Iberia) has to gain is a truly global partnership."

Iberia had to cut most of its 85 percent stake in Aerolineas Argentinas, whose losses had dragged Iberia deep into the red, along with its shares in Argentine domestic airline Austral and Chile's Ladeco. Iberia also had a holding in Venezuela's Viasa.
Chilean airline Ladeco said in April that Iberia would sell its 38 percent stake in the carrier, and shareholders in Venezuela's Viasa agreed to liquidate this loss-making airline within a year.
